subject: Question about pareto_type_2 - problem with range constraints I don't understand

messages.author: 27a3a0f42772bb11
messages.subject: Question about pareto_type_2 - problem with range constraints I don't understand
parts:
I am trying to build a model where I need - for the model - a sample from a pareto type 2 distribution.

If I run (say)

parameters {
  real <lower=0> V;
}
model {
  V ~ pareto_type_2(0, 3,3);
}

things are fine.  If I delete the <lower=0> then things are not fine: I get a blizzard of thrown exceptions.
More importantly, I would actually like to declare V as a variable in the model block (because I don't actually need it, except to start things off); i.e.

parameters {
  real W;
}
model {
 real V;
  V ~ pareto_type_2(0, 3,3);
  otherStuff(W,V);
}

but this complains bitterly.

What do I not understand?

Thanks,

Sean Matthews

P.S., most recent version of Stan (installed about 6 hours ago), running under R in Windows/32

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Question about pareto_type_2 - problem with range constraints I don't understand
parts:
Hi Sean,

You're missing a key conceptual bit of the Stan language. In the Stan language, your goal is to define a log joint probability distribution function (up to a additive constant) over the data and the parameters.

What the Stan language does not do is specify some sort of rejection sampler. That is very inefficient. This line:
  V ~ pareto_type_2(0, 3, 3);
does not mean, "please draw V from a pareto_type_2 random number generator with arguments (0, 3, 3)." It means this:
  target += pareto_type_2_lpdf(V | 0, 3, 3);
The value of target at the end of the model block is the value of the log joint probability distribution function.

If you notice in the first program, you've correctly specified data, which is nothing, parameters, V, and the log joint probability distribution function: V ~ pareto_type_2(0, 3, 3). Also notice that you haven't actually specified how to do inference. That's outside of the language. It's the job of the inference algorithm to fill in the values of each of the parameters at each iteration. To be concrete, at each iteration (and each evaluation of the log probability), the data is known, the parameters are actual values (like 0.1, 1.2, etc.), and the model block evaluates to a number.

In your second program, V is a local variable. It takes on the value of NaN without defining it. So this line:  V ~ pareto_type_2(0, 3, 3) or equivalent to target += pareto_type_2_lpdf(V | 0, 3, 3) evaluates to nonsense. Why? Maybe a simpler example from R is: rnorm(NA). What do you expect to happen?

The quick fix: move V back to parameters. Jointly estimate V and W.


Hopefully that makes sense.


Daniel

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Question about pareto_type_2 - problem with range constraints I don't understand
parts:
By "sampler view," I believe you mean "rejection sampler view." It's a common misconception and that's why we're moving away from the BUGS notation of using ~ to explicitly indicate that you are incrementing the log probability distribution function.

And... if you actually tried to do anything complex or high dimensional, rejection sampling won't get you very far.



Daniel
